population.span: we enrolled 1961 adults with a body-mass index (the weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in meters) of 30 or greater (≥27 in persons with ≥1 weight-related coexisting condition), who did not have diabetes

endpoint.span: The coprimary end points were the percentage change in body weight and weight reduction of at least 5%.

estimate.span: The mean change in body weight from baseline to week 68 was -14.9% in the semaglutide group as compared with -2.4% with placebo, for an estimated treatment difference of -12.4 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], -13.4 to -11.5; P<0.001).

ci.span: estimated treatment difference of -12.4 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], -13.4 to -11.5; P<0.001)

analysis_set.span: POPULATION: Overall number of participants analyzed = full analysis set (FAS) which comprised all randomized participants. Number Analyzed = number of participants with available data. | PARAM: MEAN | UNIT: Percentage point

treatment_strategy.span: randomly assigned them, in a 2:1 ratio, to 68 weeks of treatment with once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide (at a dose of 2.4 mg) or placebo, plus lifestyle intervention.

follow_up.span: The mean change in body weight from baseline to week 68

served_mismatch: The served row combines observed in-trial means -15.6 and -2.8 (SDs 10.1 and 6.5) with overall randomized denominators 1306 and 655. The registry gives available-data denominators 1212 and 577 for those means. These observed summaries do not reproduce the requested treatment-policy effect: the abstract reports -12.4 percentage points (95% CI -13.4 to -11.5), with arm changes -14.9% and -2.4%.
